scope: Theorem 1.1 (Interfaces and all nested loops) of the manuscript “Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4” (preprints/Square-lattice-FK-interfaces-and-nested-loops-for-1-leq-q-lt-4-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d2ffa94ece599e88), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 5-6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed real 1 ≤ q < 4, the following assertions hold. (i) For every bounded Jordan domain D with distinct boundary marks a, b, and every approximation satisfying (1.3), the Dobrushin strand ηn converges in law, in (1.4), to chordal SLEκ(q) from a to b in D. (ii) Under the specified free infinite-volume law, Γδ converges in law as δ ↓ 0 to the nested whole-plane CLEκ(q), in the spherical collection topology just defined. The limit is Möbius invariant. 5 Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence. No uniformity in q is asserted.
